statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail remains in the low band well below the block threshold, while Stress sits at the top of the elevated band on an unresolved energy, currency and rates backdrop.
recommendation: The deterministic Tail-to-action mapping resolves to EA_ON for NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD alike. A narrow danger window is flagged for the post-holiday U.S. cash reopening between 13:30 and 15:00 UTC, where two sessions of accumulated Middle East, energy and rates news are discounted in a single auction. Existing-position management and emergency protection are unaffected by this mapping.
headline: NQ holds just under its overnight high while a seven-month-high yen and lower ES and YM futures deny cross-asset alignment
body: U.S. cash equity markets were closed on Monday 7 September for Labor Day, so the Nasdaq-100 last settled a full cash session on 4 September. NQ futures trade at 29,706.25, up 0.48%, and sit just under the 29,715.25 overnight high in a band running from 29,525.00, roughly 0.64% wide. Holding close to the overnight extreme is the one mild Tail amplifier present, but the band is narrow and there is no shallow-pullback, failed-retracement or repeated-extension sequence of the kind that defines a pathological path. Cross-asset confirmation is not merely absent, it is contradictory: the yen has strengthened to 153.04 per dollar, its firmest since 18 February, on a fully priced 25 basis point Bank of Japan increase at the 17-18 September meeting and Japanese July real wages at plus 2.4%, while S&P 500 e-mini futures are down about 0.1% and Dow futures about 0.6% lower against the Nasdaq's gain. Delayed cross-asset context collected at 02:19 UTC agrees on that split, showing NQ plus 0.43% against ES minus 0.05% and YM minus 0.61%. The energy channel remains the dominant stress carrier: Brent is $97.10 and WTI $92.39, both close to three-month highs but effectively flat on the day, after weekend U.S.-Iran strikes around the Strait of Hormuz, a second strike in a month on Saudi Aramco's 400,000 barrel-per-day Jizan refinery, and Iran's new threat to target energy infrastructure across the Persian Gulf including U.S. oil and gas interests. The rates channel has firmed alongside it, with the 10-year Treasury yield near 4.788% and a September Federal Reserve increase genuinely live after August payrolls came in at 162,000 against a 55,000 consensus. The last completed cash session showed sharp internal dispersion, with semiconductors broadly higher and large-cap software and consumer names softer. The one scheduled feature that genuinely shapes the day is the 13:30 UTC cash reopening, which must discount two sessions of accumulated news in a single auction; that is reflected as a narrow conditional danger window rather than a change in the current mapped state.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock-hours were published continuously with Tail between 5 and 10 and the mapped state green throughout. Stress rose from the mid-50s during the Asian and European hours of 7 September into the low-to-mid 60s from roughly 14:00 UTC onward, as the weekend U.S.-Iran escalation and the Aramco Jizan report carried crude to multi-week highs. Confidence eased from the mid-80s to the mid-to-high 70s over the same stretch, reflecting the Labor Day cash closure and the resulting absence of U.S. cash breadth and volume evidence, then recovered to about 80 overnight as Asian trade supplied a live price path again. The dominant mode alternated between normal and mixed and at no point registered persistent directional efficiency.
outlookSummary: The 24-hour path is shaped by one dominant scheduled feature: the U.S. cash reopening at 13:30 UTC after the Labor Day closure, which must price two sessions of accumulated Middle East, energy and rates news in a single auction. Conditional Tail is held in the high single digits through the Asian and European hours, rises to a path peak of 18 in the first full hour of cash trade, then decays through the U.S. afternoon on the assumption that price discovery becomes orderly, without being decayed into the closing auction. Conditional Stress follows the same shape, moving into the high band from 08:00 UTC and easing back through the elevated band after the cash close. Every hour maps to EA_ON because no persistent no-retracement structure is observed and cross-asset confirmation is contradictory rather than aligned. The stated conditional invalidation is repeated extension after failed retracements with NQ holding near session extremes; a fresh Hormuz or Red Sea supply discontinuity and a disorderly yen carry unwind remain the identified unscheduled channels.
